summary_en: Kobe Bussan announced a 60 billion yen euro-yen convertible bond issuance with a 7-year maturity and 0% coupon, with an initial conversion price of 3,652 yen (23% premium). Concurrently, the company will repurchase up to 16 million shares or 40 billion yen through ToSTNeT-3 starting September 30, 2026, through April 30, 2027.
title_en: Supplementary Explanatory Materials Regarding Euro-Yen Convertible Bond Issuance and Share Buyback (Final Terms Version)
translation_en_brief:
On September 29, 2026, Kobe Bussan announced the issuance of a 60 billion yen convertible bond in euro-yen form with a 7-year maturity and 0% coupon. The bond carries an initial conversion price of 3,652 yen, representing a 23% premium to the closing price as of the announcement date. The bond is redeemable at par from year 5 onwards and includes a put option at 100% after 5 years. Conversion is restricted at 150% of par during the initial period through 15 months before maturity, then 130% from that point until 3 months before maturity.

Concurrently, Kobe Bussan initiated a share buyback program with a maximum outlay of 40 billion yen or 16 million shares, whichever is reached first, during the period from September 30, 2026, through April 30, 2027. The company plans to execute the buyback through ToSTNeT-3 beginning the day after the board resolution date. Should the ToSTNeT-3 purchases fall short of the 40 billion yen ceiling, the company intends to continue acquiring shares through open market purchases, subject to market conditions and applicable regulations.

The convertible bond will be offered exclusively outside the United States to investors primarily in Europe and Asia. The offering is managed by Morgan Stanley & Co. International plc as active bookrunner. The company, the Gyomu Super Japan Dream Foundation, Coccolare Inc., Hirokazu Numata, and M&U Asset Management LLC are each subject to a 180-day lock-up.
